memories.content: The user keeps a small table fan beside the bedroom window.
On a day the user drank coffee late in the afternoon, they could not fall asleep until dawn.
On a day the user drank coffee before 2 p.m., they fell asleep at their usual time.
On a tired day, the user ate dinner out and postponed even washing the dishes after returning home.
In the same week, on a day the user made simple noodles at home, they rested immediately after the meal.
On a night the window was left open, street noise woke the user twice.
On a night the table fan was running, the user was not too warm even with the window closed.
The user's father prefers to have coffee available after dinner and believes it will not cause a sleep problem.
When making a sleep-related suggestion, do not treat one or two records as a general lifestyle habit.
The user tends to go to bed much later after drinking coffee late in the afternoon.
The user keeps the shared laundry-room access card in an entrance drawer.
The user went downstairs 25 minutes after the laundry finished and received a note from another household.
For the next load, the user set a reminder five minutes before the end and removed the laundry immediately.
The user washed light-colored clothes with new jeans, and color transferred onto white socks.
The user later washed the new jeans separately, and the color of the other clothes did not change.
On a day the user did not check the dryer filter, the clothes needed another drying cycle.
On the next use, after emptying the filter, the user finished drying in one cycle.
The building manager judges that not leaving finished laundry for a long time is fair to other households.
When creating a shared laundry-room reminder, base it on the end time of the machine the user started.
Even if the local agent knows where the card is kept, it cannot know which machines in the shared laundry room are currently available.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains: bedroom sleep conditions, caffeine, meals, and inference caution on one side; shared-laundry timing, sorting, drying, access, fairness, reminders, and capability limits on the other. Neither frame supplies a scope-aligned counterpart to the other.

relations.reason: This is independently useful bedroom-equipment location information with no laundry-side counterpart.
relations.summary: A small table fan is kept beside the bedroom window.

relations.reason: The specific sleepless night and the stated recurring tendency express one underlying caffeine-timing claim, absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: Late-afternoon coffee is associated with substantially delayed sleep for the user.

relations.reason: This bounded early-coffee observation is independently useful and has no compared-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Coffee consumed before 2 p.m. coincided with the user's usual sleep time on one recorded day.

relations.reason: This isolated meal-and-chore observation has no semantically corresponding laundry claim.
relations.summary: On one tired day, eating dinner out was followed by postponing dishwashing at home.

relations.reason: This bounded home-meal observation is independent of the compared frame's laundry content.
relations.summary: On one day that week, the user made simple noodles and rested immediately after eating.

relations.reason: Both observations split one underlying bedroom cooling-and-noise claim, for which the compared frame provides no counterpart.
relations.summary: The sleep-environment records contrast open-window street-noise awakenings with comfortable temperature using a fan while the window was closed.

relations.reason: This records another person's preference and belief, with no corresponding compared-side information.
relations.summary: The user's father wants coffee available after dinner and believes it will not impair sleep.

relations.reason: This is a distinct evidentiary constraint for sleep-related guidance and has no laundry-side equivalent.
relations.summary: Sleep suggestions should not generalize one or two records into a lifestyle habit.

relations.reason: This is independently useful access-item location information absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: The shared laundry-room access card is kept in an entrance drawer.

relations.reason: The two events split one underlying claim about reminder-supported prompt collection, with no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: A delayed laundry pickup drew a household note, while an advance reminder enabled immediate pickup on the next load.

relations.reason: The paired wash outcomes express one underlying sorting-and-dye-transfer claim absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: New jeans transferred color when washed with light clothes, whereas separating them avoided color changes to other clothes.

relations.reason: The paired drying outcomes split one underlying filter-related efficiency claim with no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Skipping the dryer-filter check coincided with needing another cycle, while emptying it preceded completion in one cycle.

relations.reason: This shared-facility fairness judgment is independently useful and absent from the reference frame.
relations.summary: The building manager considers avoiding long delays in removing finished laundry fair to other households.

relations.reason: This operational reminder rule has no scope-aligned claim in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Shared laundry-room reminders should be based on the end time of the machine the user started.

relations.reason: This capability boundary is independently useful and has no reference-side counterpart.
relations.summary: Knowing the access-card location does not provide knowledge of current shared laundry-machine availability.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers laundry access, prompt collection, dye-transfer prevention, dryer-filter effects, shared-room fairness, reminder timing, and lack of live machine-availability knowledge.
reports.reference_only: The reference records bedroom cooling and noise, caffeine timing and sleep, isolated meal-and-rest observations, a family preference, and caution against generalizing sparse records.
